newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir cosmonauts face power problems after collision.
newsitem.headline: Mir cosmonauts face power problems after collision.

text.p: Cosmonauts on board Russia's Mir space station said on Wednesday they were facing power problems after their ageing vessel collided with a cargo craft during a manual docking exercise.

Mission control director Vladimir Lobachyov, speaking after liaising with the three-man Mir crew, told reporters the collision was "the most serious accident in recent times" and said it may have been the result of a technical malfunction.

The unmanned Progress cargo craft collided with the Spektr scientific module Spektr attached to the main section of Mir at 1.20 p.m. (0920 GMT), causing a partial loss of air pressure. Mission control officials have made clear the cosmonauts are not in any immediate danger because of the collision.

"The cosmonauts say that on Mir there is a fall in the electrical supply...and as a result of the collision a hole (in Spektr) has developed whose size is still unclear," Lobachyov told a news briefing at the mission control centre just outside Moscow.
Mir is manned by U.S. astronaut Michael Foale, who reached the station on the space shuttle Atlantis in May and was to stay until September, and Russians Vasily Tsibliyev and Alexander Lazutkin.

Lobachyov said a commission would decide Spektr's fate and added that it might be undocked from the space station. Progress, which is gradually moving away from Mir, is expected to fall to Earth and sink into the Pacific Ocean on Friday.
